question: The National Commission on Agriculture (1976) of India has classified social forestry into how many categories?
solution:
The correct answer is__** 3.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **Social forestry** is divided into **three categories** by the **National Commission on Agriculture(1976).**
 
• These three types of forestry are** farm, rural, and urban.**
 
• **Urban forestry**:
 
 
• It is the practice of** growing and maintaining trees **on** public and privately owned properties** in and near urban areas, such as greenways, parks, avenues along streets, and green spaces for industry and commerce, among other places.
 
 
 
• **Rural forestry:**
 
 
• **Agroforestry and community forestry **are promoted heavily in rural forestry.
 
• Agro-forestry is the practice of **growing food and trees on the same land,** including unused areas.
 
• It alters the **simultaneous production of food, fodder, fuel, timber, and fruit** by combining forestry and agriculture.
 
• Growing trees on** public or communal land**, such as schoolyards, highway ditches, canal banks, village pastures, and temple grounds, is known as** community forestry.**
 
 
 
• **Farm forestry:**
 
 
• Farmers are urged to plant trees on their **property to meet their family's domestic requirements.**
 
• This custom of **cultivating trees on farmland **is widespread and already in place.
 
• Farmers can use** waste land for soil conservation, wind shelters, or to offer shade** for their crops.
